regime.summary: Policy rate held at 10.5% but bills price hikes: 6M cutoff 0.65pp above policy, CPI up 1.7pp in three months, Brent +64% in three months. Index bounced 11.6% in a month after a 9.1% three-month fall, so the rebound is partly done. Tightening plus oil shock resembles the 2021-22 episode, but only partly; no timing edge is claimed.

Tightening plus external stress: rate up 800bp in ten months with CPI above it.

exposure_reason: Below the 75% default by 20 points, argued on regime rather than timing: bills price hikes (6M cutoff 0.65pp over policy), CPI is rising, Brent is up 64% in three months, and the index has already bounced 11.6% in a month, which is the shape of the tightening-plus-stress episode in situations.md. Not zero: no timing edge is measured, the core rests on business and earnings, and the oil-linked name hedges the shock. The 45% reserve is for a hike-driven drop or a new live opportunity; I would return to 75% if bills ease or the MPC holds.
not_known: Reserves, current account and IMF status are not in the bundle. No business-quality, sponsor or balance-sheet facts exist for GHNI or IPAK, so those weights rest on reported EPS and P/E only. Consolidated versus unconsolidated EPS is unknown.
contamination_note: I have some general recollection of the period after 2026-04-24 and discarded it; no figure or judgment here uses it. base_rates.csv warns it is measured past this date, so I cited none of its numbers and relied on screens, market.md, situations.md and questions.md only.
